dimensions.name: Question Quality
dimensions.measures: Do the student's questions move beyond recall toward analysis?

levels.1: Asks only what the content already states.
levels.3: Asks why or how something happened.
levels.4: Asks a question that targets the weakest part of the argument.

dimensions.name: Evidence and Reasoning
dimensions.measures: Are claims tied to specific evidence in the content?

levels.1: Offers opinion with no reference to the content.
levels.2: Refers to the content in general terms.
levels.3: Cites a specific number, passage, or visual detail.
levels.4: Weighs whether the cited evidence actually supports the claim.

dimensions.name: Assumption Awareness
dimensions.measures: Does the student surface unstated assumptions?

levels.2: Expresses vague doubt without naming the assumption.
levels.3: Names an unstated assumption such as correlation implying causation.
levels.4: Names the assumption and explains what evidence would test it.

dimensions.name: Depth of Follow-up
dimensions.measures: Does each turn build on the previous exchange rather than restart?

levels.1: Each message is unrelated to the last.
levels.2: Repeats or lightly rephrases an earlier point.
levels.3: Extends the previous idea with a new angle.
levels.4: Revises an earlier position in light of new reasoning.

dimensions.name: Synthesis
dimensions.measures: Does the student form a new position or connection?

levels.2: Restates the content's conclusion as their own.
levels.3: States a qualified position of their own.
levels.4: Proposes an alternative explanation or a way to test the claim.
